propositions: Bridge orchestration must be implemented as a runner-neutral packaged Python core exposed through all three public interfaces: Python library (rebar.bridge_run), CLI (rebar bridge run), and MCP (write-gated bridge_run tool).

The packaged runner must accept five profiles (reconcile-check, dry-run, bootstrap-strict, bootstrap-throttle, live) that map to legacy rebar reconcile and rebar bridge commands while remaining available through pip wheel, Homebrew wheel-backed, and MCP Registry/uvx install paths.

Provider workflows must retain MODE environment variable compatibility while public surfaces use the canonical noun profile; direct legacy reconcile callers preserve benign results 3/4/75 while the new runner maps benign legacy results to canonical success 0.

The runner must validate environments, enforce 3600-second timeout, validate pause markers, translate provider results, and perform strict ticket-store delivery with run id and bot identity; delivery failure returns exit code 1 with diagnostics.

GitHub Actions, Jenkins, and GitLab provider wrappers must invoke exactly rebar bridge run without repository-local scripts; GitLab schema must be vendored with validated immutable upstream revision and SHA-256 provenance, and embedded shell must pass pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0 linting.

Explicit repo_root parameter overrides inherited REBAR_ROOT; shallow repositories return invalid invocation code before reconciliation; all acceptance criteria and interface-parity tests must pass without deferred findings.
